title: Compactification of an affine scheme
statement:
Let $X$ be an affine scheme of finite type over a field $K$. There
is an open dense immersion $X\to\bar X$ with $\bar X$ projective
over $K$ (choose a closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_K$, take the scheme-theoretic closure in $\mathbf P^n_K$); one
has $\kundim\bar X=\kundim X$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-chow-affine-immersion] with $Y=\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $U=X$. It supplies a finite number $n$ of algebra generators, the closed immersion $e:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_K$ induced by the corresponding polynomial-algebra surjection, and its composite immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_K$ through the standard open $D_+(x_0)=\mathbf A^n_K$. All these maps are over $K$.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: polynomial presentation and the standard affine chart; compare Stacks Tag 0200, proof step 3

proof.text: The finite-type hypothesis makes $X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; taking the preimage of the entire affine base shows that $X$ is quasi-compact. The base $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is affine by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Thus [lem-chow-closed-model] applies to the immersion $j$ of step 1. Set $\bar X=\operatorname{SIm}(j)$, the scheme-theoretic closure in $\mathbf P^n_K$ supplied by the closed-model statement. The cited closed-model statement gives the factorization $X\xrightarrow{a}\bar X\xrightarrow{i}\mathbf P^n_K$, with $a$ a scheme-theoretically dense open immersion, $i$ a closed immersion, and $\bar X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ proper. Its structure morphism is the composite with the projective-space projection, so $a$ is over $K$. Properness of $\bar X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ includes separatedness by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. In the commutative triangle $X\xrightarrow{a}\bar X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, the source structure map is of finite type and $a$ is an open immersion. Therefore [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target] makes $a$ quasi-compact, checking the hypothesis of the density definition used in step 3.

source.place: Tag 01RG, lemma-quasi-compact-immersion; Tag 01WC, lemma-locally-projective-proper; blueprint proof, closure sentence

proof.text: The scheme-theoretic density in step 2 means that $\mathcal O_{\bar X}\to a_*\mathcal O_X$ is injective, as specified in [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open]. This implies topological density directly: if the complement of the closure of $a(X)$ were nonempty, choose a nonempty affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ inside that complement, using the local affine description of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Then $a^{-1}(W)=\varnothing$, so injectivity on sections would give an injective map $A=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to\Gamma(\varnothing,\mathcal O_X)=0$. Hence $A=0$, whose spectrum is empty by [def-weil-affine-spectrum], contradicting the choice of $W$. Thus $a(X)$ is dense in $\bar X$. This is also the topological-density conclusion of Stacks Tag 01RG, proved here rather than assumed from a definition.

source.place: Tag 01RG, lemma-quasi-compact-immersion, final assertion (elementary implication from the supplied sheaf injection)

proof.text: The closed immersion $i:\bar X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_K$ of step 2, followed by its structural projection to $\operatorname{Spec}K$, is exactly the finite-projective-space embedding required by [def-kun-projective]. Consequently $\bar X$ is projective over $K$. Its properness was supplied in step 2; by [def-weil-proper-morphism], properness includes finite type. In particular $\bar X$ is of finite type over the same field $K$, as needed for the dimension assertion.

source.place: Proof, closed-subscheme hence projective sentence; Stacks Tag 01W1, definition-proper

proof.text: Apply the dense-open clause of [lem-kun-dimension-extension] to the finite-type $K$-scheme $\bar X$ from step 4 and the open immersion $a:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ from step 2, whose topological density was proved in step 3. It gives $\kundim X=\kundim\bar X$. Reversing this equality proves the last clause of the item. Together with the construction and projectivity above this proves every assertion, including the indicated choice of the scheme-theoretic closure.

source.place: Tag 0A21, lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic, items (3) and (8); blueprint proof, final dimension sentence
